An illustration of an Ekpe masquerader in a traditional raffia costume, holding a staff and a bell. The costume should be colourful with geometric patterns, completely covering the person, with a large, elaborate raffia mane around the neck. Beside him, an Efik chief in traditional 19th-century wealthy attire (a top hat, a long wrapper, and a staff) standing respectfully.

Map of the south-eastern Nigeria coast in the 19th century, showing the Cross River estuary. The towns of Duke Town, Creek Town, Henshaw Town, and Obutong should be marked together as "Old Calabar". Inland, mark the territories of the Ibibio, Annang, Ekoi (Ejagham), and Igbo. Arrows should point from the hinterland to Old Calabar and from the coast inland.
